I've been experimenting with https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-blueprint (which states that it is a temporary mirror for the for now unavailable https://github.com/leanprover/verso-blueprint). It looks really promising!
I have several questions and remarks:

  1. Can we make sub-groups? I tried adding a parent argument to a group, but that's an error.
  2. Is there an option to prune transitive dependencies in the graph? My current graph is a mess full of arrows because my dependencies were generated by leanArchitect, so each lemma refers to every definition it needs.
  3. It would be very nice to have a great feature from LeanArchitect: detect the dependencies from the Lean.
  4. While the graphs for each group and the graph of groups look nice, the full graph feels too horizontal. The groups tend to be all side by side and there are long horizontal dependencies arrow.
  5. Can we reference a definition or lemma outside of a def/lemma environment? {uses "name"}[] does not work in free text.
  6. I have a few maxRecDepth errors when I add a (lean := "My.Lemma.name") to lemmas, which prevent me from linking the Lean (on 3 out of around 100 lemmas, for no reason that I can see). I'll give a precise example once my blueprint is publicly accessible.
  7. I am translating a latex blueprint, and I sometimes have an align environment with several lines and & alignment characters. It looks like the verso $$ environment does not support that. Is there a way to write multiple lines of maths with alignment in verso?

@Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias

Hi @Rémy Degenne, sorry for the delayed reply. We have been ironing out a few issues before a wider release, but the code now seems ready. Note that the code is now in the leanprover GitHub organization.

  1. Absolutely. We opted for having only two levels because that maps directly to the dot rendering model, but we’d be happy to extend the parent attribute to both regular nodes and group nodes. Could you say a bit more about the structure of your blueprint? How many levels do you expect to have?

  2. Not yet, but we’d be happy to add support for it. It’d be helpful if you could point us to a concrete test case in your blueprint, so we can make sure we support your needs properly.

  3. Indeed! We’re currently missing some controls for this analysis, especially around how it can be configured and inspected. I’ll prioritize adding those controls and documenting the available options.

  4. Recent versions provide some more graph-control primitives, such as direction and pack. They can be set at compile time or interactively in the graph browser. Please don’t hesitate to request more features in this area, either here or by opening an issue in the VBP repository.

  5. You can use {bpref "label"} inside or outside nodes to create a reference that doesn’t register a uses edge. I’d be happy to allow uses outside nodes too, but we’d need to define the semantics.

  6. Yes, please — that would be very helpful.

  7. This should work. Let me look into it; there may be a bug in the VBP LaTeX code.

Thanks for the answers!
For the subgroups, I would need 2 levels, 3 max. I discovered I wanted subgroups because I had a group about an algorithm, and I wanted a subgroup for its definition+API, and another subgroup for a theorem I proved about it.
Sounds good. I'd target a node , group, supergroup design. I'll look into dot a bit more to see how that could be rendered, but worst case we just render 2 levels at a time.

We just started using @Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias's new verso-blueprint package for a formalization project at our Lean seminar at CWI / University of Amsterdam. Here is the HTML blueprint and the GitHub repo.
